title: Edge Normalizers: Field Guide (draft)
content:
Quick personal field guide for labelers + engineers when we hit weird normalized values in user data. This is a scratch/draft — still lots of open questions, examples, and heuristics to validate on samples. Purpose: consolidate consistent normalizers and labeling rules we keep re-writing in ad-hoc PRs. Keep short, pragmatic rules + example-driven decisions.

1) Scope / motivation
- Problem: inconsistent tokens introduced by localization, punctuation, and encoding cause labeler disagreement and model drift (esp. NER, phone/email extraction, currency spans).
- Goal: provide lightweight normalizers and label-preserving heuristics to reduce noise before labeling, and explicit rules about "what to label" vs "what to normalize first".
- Non-goal: exhaustive locale formatting engine — we prefer heuristics that fix the 90% painful cases and leave remainder for annotator abstain + annotation notes.

2) High-level rules (short)
- Prefer canonical unicode normalization (NFKC) for storage, but keep original raw text preserved for audit. Do not NFKC when it changes semantic whitespace or hidden script content (see examples).
- Lowercase for labeler view only for case-insensitive entity classes (emails, urls, vat codes). Keep case in final stored span for recoverability unless labeler explicitly says "case matters".
- Normalize common punctuation sequences (e.g., em-dash variants -> " - ") before tokenization. Document all changes in metadata.
- Always preserve contiguous span offsets: normalizer should provide mapping from normalized indices back to original indices. If mapping ambiguous, mark example for manual review.

3) Unicode surprises and heuristics
- Full-width vs half-width digits (e.g., １２３ vs 123): convert to ASCII digits when inside numeric-looking sequences unless adjacent CJK characters suggest cultural context.
- Combining diacritics vs composed forms: NFKC recommended; but for named entities in languages that distinguish diacritics semantically (Polish, Turkish), flag for reviewer if normalization collapses to ambiguous base.
- Directional overrides (RLM/LRM) can silently change span boundaries. Strip control characters unless evidence they mark meaningful grouping (rare).
- Right-to-left script + punctuation: preserve original order when providing labeler UI; normalized text for model training can reorder but store mapping.

4) Numbers, currencies, and separators
- Prefer to normalize thousands separators and decimal separators to a canonical internal form for numeric extraction ("1,234.56" -> "1234.56"), but keep original string as provenance.
- Locale rule: if both "," and "." present, infer locale by pattern (e.g., "1.234,56" -> European). If ambiguous ("1,234"), do NOT normalize automatically — mark as ambiguous and present both parses to labeler.
- Currency symbols: if symbol attached to number ("$1,200" vs "1.200 kr"), normalize to 3 fields: symbol, numeric_value (canonical), annotated_span. When symbol is wordy ("US dollars"), treat as separate token unless contiguous.

5) Phone numbers and contact spans
- Normalize to E.164 when country context available; otherwise preserve original. Only transform if country prefix present or metadata supplies country.
- Remove visual separators (spaces, dots, parentheses) when computing digit-based heuristics, but show original to labelers.
- For ambiguous short sequences ("555-1234"), label as LOCAL_PHONE and keep original form; do not force country-level normalization.

6) Emails, urls, and ids
- Lowercase domains, keep local-part casing as-is in stored raw text. For label spans, domain-only match ok.
- When tokenization splits urls across soft-breaks, glue back using URL-detection regex before labeling. Provide a preview of normalized url for labeler confirmation.

7) Overlapping / nested spans policy
- Prefer longest-first for atomic entity types (ORG, PRODUCT) unless shorter span has different type that would be lost (PERSON inside ORG). In those cases allow nested spans and mark relation.
- For ambiguous overlapping mentions caused by punctuation normalization (e.g., "ACME, Inc." -> "ACME Inc"), keep both candidate spans and present to reviewer with suggestion to merge.

8) Partial labels & abstain guidance
- If more than two plausible normalizations for a numeric/currency/phone span, labeler should mark as ABSTAIN and add a short rationale in comment. We will treat ABSTAIN examples as high-priority for adjudication sampling.
- Use "partial-span" tag when only a portion of a value is confidently labeled (e.g., area code only). Avoid creating new entity types for partials; use span-level attributes.

9) Practical heuristics and quick rules for labelers (cheat-sheet)
- If you can read it unambiguously as a single number after removing separators -> normalize and label as NUMBER/CURRENCY.
- If punctuation ambiguity affects type ("1,234" could be one thousand two-hundred or one point two three four) -> mark ambiguous and add comment.
- If diacritics remove identity (two different people become same string after normalization) -> do not normalize; ask for adjudication sample.
- For unknown country phone numbers: keep original, label as CONTACT:PHONE-UNK.

10) QA sampling plan (operational)
- Build a periodic sample of 500 examples where normalization changed byte-level text. Priority: currency/phone/NER-critical classes.
- Track disagreement rate vs previous week; if >8% labeler disagreement on normalized examples, freeze automatic normalization and escalate.

11) Implementation notes for engineers
- Normalizer MUST emit reversible mapping: list of tuples "(orig_start, orig_end) -> (norm_start, norm_end)" serialized in sample metadata. If impossible, return "mapping_conflict":true and do not auto-normalize.
- Provide a flag to labeler UI: show "raw / normalized" toggles. Default to showing normalized but with raw available on hover.
- Keep normalization configuration as code (yaml) with versioning; tag dataset exports with normalizer version.

12) Open questions / TODOs
- Q: When is NFKC dangerous for short alphanumeric ids (SÅS vs SAS)? Need sample audit in airline dataset.
- Q: Edge-case numbers embedded in product SKUs ("AB-12,34") — do we ever split? Suggest treat as textual SKUs unless explicit numeric intent.
- TODO: bake a small locale-detection heuristic in preprocessor to reduce ambiguous numeric parses.
- TODO: add 200 real examples for each ambiguous class and run round-robin labeler validation.

13) Quick example bank (for training labelers)
- "Invoice № 12A/2020" -> keep "№" and numeric sequence; label "12A/2020" as INVOICE_ID, do not strip slash.
- "€1.234,56" -> normalize numeric_value: 1234.56, currency: EUR, original: "€1.234,56".
- "⒈ Appendix" (circled numbers) -> convert circled digits to ascii digits for numeric tokens, but show original.
- "محمد علي" vs "Mohamed Ali" -> do not normalize across scripts; treat as distinct mentions unless alias dataset says otherwise.

14) Notes to self / process reminders
- Communicate changes in normalizer via weekly "data-ops" note and include before/after diffs for first 2 weeks of rollout.
- When changing normalizer version, create an "adjudication sweep" dataset: examples where previous and new normalization disagree. Prioritize product-critical customers.

If anything below looks too formal or misses nuance, flag me. Will iterate after sampling 2k examples.

-- Maya
